#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH] [--define NAME]...
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR;
#                                             --define adds -DNAME (test
#                                             builds only, tools/perf.py)
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src defines=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --define)
                case "$2" in
                    ''|*[!A-Z0-9_]*) echo "build: --define takes a NAME of A-Z, 0-9 and _" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                defines="$defines $2"; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "build: --out DIR is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    tag=$(image_tag)
    docker image inspect "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cmd_image
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e SB_DEFINES="$defines" \
        -v "$ROOT:$src_mount:ro" -v "$out:/out" -w "$src_mount" \
        "$tag" sh "$src_mount/tools/build.sh" inside "$src_mount" /out
    cat "$out/SHA256SUMS"
}

# The image's size in bytes, from the symbols firmware/app.ld defines:
# code (code and constants, in the image), data (initialised data: in the
# image and copied to RAM), bss (zeroed RAM, the beacon included), image
# (the raw image's length), stack (reserved at the top of RAM, both
# stacks) and irq_stack (the lower part of it: the interrupt stack).
write_size() {
    sym() { nm "$1" | awk -v s="$2" '$3 == s { print $1 }'; }
    hex() { printf '%d' "0x$1"; }
    origin=$(hex 02000000)
    data_load=$(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_load)")
    data=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_start)") ))
    bss=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_start)") ))
    stack=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    irq=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __irq_stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    printf 'code %d\ndata %d\nbss %d\nimage %d\nstack %d\nirq_stack %d\n' \
        $((data_load - origin)) "$data" "$bss" $((data_load - origin + data)) "$stack" "$irq"
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
            -Ifirmware/src -Ivendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -D$d"; done
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -nostdinc -Werror"
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    # Objects are intermediate: kept out of the outputs.
    obj=/tmp/small-beeps-obj
    rm -rf "$obj" && mkdir -p "$obj"
    objs=""
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -T firmware/app.ld \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs
    # The raw image is the code, then the initial data, which app.ld loads
    # right after it. This objcopy takes one section at a time, and ld's
    # own binary output gets data addresses wrong, so the two are joined.
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app.elf" "$obj/text.bin"
    objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$obj/data.bin"
    cat "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin" > "$out/app.bin"
    rm "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin"
    set +x
    write_size "$out/app.elf" > "$out/app.size"
    cat "$out/app.size"
    image=$(awk '$1 == "image" { print $2 }' "$out/app.size")
    if [ "$(wc -c < "$out/app.bin")" -ne "$image" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: app.bin is not the $image bytes app.ld lays out" >&2; exit 1
    fi
    # No output may contain the absolute source path.
    for f in $(find "$out" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        if grep -q -F "$src" "$f"; then
            echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $src" >&2; exit 1
        fi
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Runs fwtest from its published container image, pinned by digest in
# config/fwtest-image (R-SEP-3). The firmware side uses the harness only
# this way: docs/HARNESS.md is the manual.
#
#   tools/fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
#   tools/fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
#   tools/fwtest version
#   tools/fwtest --image          print the pinned image reference
#
# The current directory is mounted read-only at /work, and every path
# argument must be inside it (relative, or absolute under it). The --out
# folder is created on the host and mounted read-write on its own. The
# container runs as linux/amd64 with no network, as your user. After a run,
# DIR/runner.txt names the image used, for the record.
#
# FWTEST_IMAGE overrides the pinned image (spec side, to try a local build);
# runner.txt then says the image was not the pinned one.
set -eu
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PIN_FILE="$ROOT/config/fwtest-image"
pinned=$(grep -v '^#' "$PIN_FILE" | grep . | head -1)
if [ -n "${FWTEST_IMAGE:-}" ]; then
    ref=$FWTEST_IMAGE
    note="not the pinned image (FWTEST_IMAGE); pinned: $pinned"
else
    case "$pinned" in
        *@sha256:????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????) ;;
        *) echo "tools/fwtest: no published image is pinned yet (config/fwtest-image: $pinned)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
    ref=$pinned
    note="pinned (config/fwtest-image)"
fi
if [ "${1:-}" = "--image" ]; then

usage: perf.py [-h] {check,probes,history,summary} ...

Measures the firmware's size, RAM and speed, and gates them (checks
C-PERF and C-PERF-PROBES; R-PERF-1 to R-PERF-5).

  perf.py check --build DIR --out DIR [--base-ref REF] [--records-ref REF]
                [--require-records]
      Measures DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output), finds the latest
      record of a main commit (the first-parent history of --base-ref,
      default origin/main, on --records-ref, default origin/records),
      measures that record's own app.bin the same way, and applies the
      gates. Writes OUT/perf.json. Exit status 1 if a gate failed.
  perf.py probes --build DIR --out DIR
      Builds the firmware with SB_PROBE_SLOW, SB_PROBE_BIG and (since
      M4b) SB_PROBE_LOADED (firmware/src/probe.c), measures each, and
      checks that the gates fail each one for its own reason, measured
      against DIR/app.bin: the slower build its speed and its steady-state
      budget, the bigger build each size budget and its startup budget,
      the loaded build its loaded speed and loaded budget, with the
      unmodified build's measurements as those budgets. Builds it also with SB_PROBE_STACK
      and checks the stack's high-water mark shows at least the 1 KiB that
      build is known to use.
      Exit status 1 if any gate did not fail as it should.
  perf.py history --record REPORT.json --csv FILE [--measures FILE]
      Appends the record's line to perf-history.csv (records workflow),
      and since M4b its rows to perf-measures.csv, one per measure. Never
      rewrites either file; a commit (and measure) that already has a
      line is left.
  perf.py summary --record REPORT.json
      Prints the record's performance as Markdown (for the CI summary).

What is measured (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M0e):
- size: code, data, bss, the raw image and the stack reserved, from
  app.size; static RAM is data + bss;
- the stack's high-water mark: the firmware fills its unused stack with
  STACK_FILL once at startup (crt0.S, sb_stack_fill), so the deepest the
  stack went is the lowest word no longer holding it, in the stack
  captured at the end of the run. An image without the fill (an older
  record's) is read by the lowest non-zero word, as fwtest starts RAM at
  zero; that method can't see words written as zero;

    the firmware's work timed on whole seconds or tenths of a second
    falls near its ends (an end can come up to about 30 ms late while the
    image idles, docs/HARNESS.md "Time");
  - startup: the instructions of the shorter run beyond its periods at the
    steady-state rate, the one-off work before the firmware settles.
  The stack's high-water mark is read at the end of the longer run.
  Until M2 speed was the instructions of one one-second run divided by
  its beats, startup included;

  input script LOAD_SCRIPT, which drives the firmware to its heaviest
  steady load (every voice sounding, every control moving), and its

  (`loaded_per_period`) is optional: a milestone without one has the

record before that budget was raised (the raise's own merge, or any merge

and the baseline note names it (choose_baseline). A fall of
more than that is reported as an improvement. Startup has its budget but

change of the firmware.

by the same rule keyed on the loaded budget, so it may be another

content.content:
47 872.34 Hz; ours is 44 117.647 Hz, so the demo raises every note by
    12 log2(47 872.34 / 44 117.647) = 1.414 semitones. Its time constants
    run 7.8% slow. A block is four renders of 16 frames (Plaits takes up
    to 24).
- **Found on the way:** a Plaits source no header names (the speech
  synthesiser's phoneme table) was missed by the include walk that chose
  the files, and was added when the first link asked for it.
  ALGORITHM is fwtest's encoder 1, not 2 (HW-39), which the first live
  check got wrong. C-SEP-TERMS flagged identifiers in Plaits' MIT code
  that also occur in the emulator's source; with the owner's approval the
  vendored Plaits' terms now count as public like the SDK's (R-SEP-1).
- **Hardware float:** the toolchain has single-precision float
  instructions (its `fprev1` feature). fwtest runs them, and the SDK's
  own AC791N builds use them (`-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1`, P-29), but
  HARDWARE-SPEC.md says nothing yet: SR-5 asks. So the demo's default is
  soft-float; `PLAITS_HWFLOAT` builds Plaits with the instructions for
  the measurements. Every engine gives the same sound bit for bit either
  way (the bench's checksums): two independent float paths agree.

### 2026-10-23 M4b: what Plaits costs, engine by engine
- **Method** (firmware/demos/plaits/bench.c, check C-PLAITS-BENCH): in
  main, before interrupts, each engine renders one block after it is
  selected (its set-up, reported apart), then four blocks at each of nine
  settings (HARMONICS, TIMBRE and MORPH each at 0 and 1, and all at 0.5),
  a key struck at the first of each. Each block is timed with the time
  base, read only before and after it, and converted at 10 cycles a tick;
  in fwtest an instruction is a cycle. Cross-check: on the live
  hardware-float demo, fwtest's own count is 30 581 a block on engine 0
  against the bench's 28 832 plus the firmware's 1 813 at rest.
- **Results**, instructions a block (64 frames; core 0 has 348 160),
  heaviest of the nine settings:
  keeps its state in globals, and two voices on two cores can't share
  one function cleanly. Add a `void *` to the engine call.
- **Knobs as parameters.** `input_value()` gives an encoder's raw detents
  since start, unbounded; the demo maps them to 0 to 1 itself. A small
  layer giving each knob a clamped parameter, and a pickup of the pot,
  would save every engine the same code.
- **A deadline the engine can see.** An engine that overruns has no way
  to know: the audio record's fill times are tests' data, not API. Give
  the engine its last fill time against the block, so it can shed voices
  before underruns start, and protect main, which starves when the
  engine overloads core 0.
- **Core 1 as an API.** The bench drives core 1 by hand (its start word,
  `C1_CON`, a RAM flag). M5 needs a small, tested way to start it, post a
  job each block and wait for it, once SR-6 says what the chip needs.
- **Floats:** if SR-5 confirms the instructions, build the firmware with
  `-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1` like the SDK, and the soft-float runtime stays a
  demo's.

heaviest of the nine settings:

  | # | Engine | Soft-float | Hardware float | Voices on core 0 (hardware float, at rest) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | virtual analog VCF | 1 005 730 | 29 150 | 11 |
  | 1 | phase distortion | 1 149 230 | 40 840 | 8 |
  | 2-4 | six-op FM (3 banks) | 818 620 to 828 930 | 30 510 to 30 760 | 11 |
  | 5 | wave terrain | 1 141 280 | 29 910 | 11 |
  | 6 | string machine | 1 215 960 | 40 510 | 8 |
  | 7 | chiptune | 184 280 | 10 560 | 32 |
  | 8 | virtual analog | 864 760 | 32 490 | 10 |
  | 9 | waveshaping | 751 790 | 19 490 | 17 |
  | 10 | FM | 1 122 150 | 41 400 | 8 |
  | 11 | grain | 1 023 190 | 28 590 | 12 |
  | 12 | additive | 1 679 090 | 45 790 | 7 |
  | 13 | wavetable | 1 291 050 | 30 680 | 11 |
  | 14 | chords | 1 139 300 | 35 620 | 9 |
  | 15 | speech | 888 940 | 26 330 | 13 |
  | 16 | swarm | 1 073 190 | 28 200 | 12 |
  | 17 | noise | 1 039 740 | 48 390 | 7 |
  | 18 | particle | 1 184 630 | 47 720 | 7 |
  | 19 | string | 1 126 800 | 38 540 | 8 |
  | 20 | modal | 1 838 260 | 52 640 | 6 |
  | 21 | bass drum | 922 440 | 27 000 | 12 |
  | 22 | snare drum | 1 031 790 | 35 080 | 9 |
  | 23 | hi-hat | 627 640 | 25 210 | 13 |

  (The record's table, from tools/plaits-bench.py, has the means, the
  set-up blocks, and voices under the heaviest input too.)
- **What the bench holds fixed:** one pitch (MIDI 48, plus the rate
  offset) and decay 0.5, so an engine whose cost grows with pitch may cost
  more higher up. The voices column counts time only. Each voice is about
  29.5 KB of RAM (its 16 KiB buffer and Plaits' voice object: the demo's
  zeroed data is 59 160 bytes more than the firmware's, for two). The
  chip's 511 KiB of RAM, less the firmware's 124 KB and its stacks, holds
  about 13 voices, fewer than the column for the lightest engines.
- **Soft-float doesn't fit.** Every engine but chiptune takes two to five
  blocks' time for one block, so only chiptune plays live with soft-float.
  Any other overloads core 0: underruns, and main starves. Soft-float is
  about 30 times slower than the instructions (18 to 39 times, by engine).
- **Clean audio:** over the whole bench soft-float raised no invalid
  operation, no overflow and no bad conversion, so Plaits made no NaN and
  no infinity. Some engines reach full scale at extreme settings (chords
  33 samples, modal 23, bass drum 149, snare 3, noise 1, of 2 304 a
  setting run): Plaits' own output stage saturating on purpose (its
  `Clip16`), not an overflow. Live, with a key held: the soft-float demo
  on chiptune, and the hardware-float demo on engine 0, with no underrun.
- **Core 1** (HW-9, HW-10): started from the bench on a loop that renders
  a second voice whenever core 0 sets a word in RAM. Two voices at once
  take 0.49 to 0.50 of the time of one after the other with hardware
  float (speed-up 1.99 to 2.02), 0.51 to 0.59 with soft-float. The
  comparison is of successive blocks, so it is good to a few percent.
  fwtest models no contention between the cores; SR-6 asks what the chip
  costs, and what core 1 needs before it runs from a raw image.

### 2026-10-23 M4b: the headroom it implies for M5
- **A frequency-modulation operator:** Plaits' six-op engine plays two
  six-operator voices, 768 operator-samples a block, for 30 550
  instructions with hardware float: at most 40 an operator-sample, its
  envelopes, low-pass gate and limiter included. M4's fixed-point sine
  oscillator (interpolated table, envelope) is 25.6 a sample. With
  soft-float it is about 1 070: soft-float is out for M5's engine.
- **At 44 117.647 Hz, 64-frame blocks:** core 0 has 348 160 cycles a
  block; the firmware takes 1 813 at rest and 114 173 under the heaviest
  input (the loaded measure, M4b), most of it main redrawing the panel.
  - **One core:** about 346 000 a block at rest, 234 000 under load:
    8 600 or 5 800 operator-samples a block, that is **135 or 91
    operators** (at 40 each; 210 or 140 at M4's 25.6), for example 22 or
    15 six-operator voices.
  - **Two cores:** core 1 adds a whole 348 000 (it does no input or
    drawing): about **8 700 more operator-samples a block, 135 more
    operators**, if the chip runs both cores like fwtest (SR-6).
  - These are fwtest's numbers, an instruction a cycle. On the chip, code
    run from flash through the cache will take more; a probe on the chip
    is still to come. Leave M5 a wide margin: plan for half.
- **For M5's design:** fixed point (as M4's oscillator) costs about what
  hardware float does in fwtest, and needs no answer from SR-5; floats
  need SR-5 to say the chip has them. The screen, not the sound, is the
  heaviest user of core 0 under input: M5's screen should redraw only
  what changed, at a bounded rate.

### 2026-10-23 M4b: the loaded measure, broken down (the owner's question)
- **Method:** the M4 firmware under the loaded script (#57's
  `tests/fw/scripts/perfload.txt`), core 0's instructions between the 1 250
  and 2 250 ms runs, over the blocks that second holds (689.3), in builds
  that each leave one part out: the existing cost builds (`SB_COST_*`), and
  two measurement-only switches added to `panel.c` for these runs and not
  committed (one skipping the panel's drawing and sending, one drawing
  without sending). Taking differences:

  | Part | Instructions a block | Share |
  |---|---|---|
  | Screen: drawing into the frame buffer (main, `panel_serve`) | 102 437 | 89.8% |
  | Screen: sending the changed rows (`lcd_send_rows`, DMA started, waited for) | 1 104 | 1.0% |
  | Audio engine (the test instrument, four voices and the tone) | 8 309 | 7.3% |
  | Input scan (keys, encoders, pot, LEDs; LEDs 215 of it) | 1 861 | 1.6% |
  | Audio output path (the interrupt, its checks, the stores) | 302 | 0.3% |
  | The tick, main's wakes and the rest | 104 | 0.1% |
  | **Total** (114 173 by the record's count of blocks) | **114 117** | |

  The scan's share is the "no panel" build less the build with no scan as
  well, less the audio engine's (with no scan no note sounds).
- **The screen dominates, and it is the drawing, not the sending.** The
  panel already redraws only the region an event touches (a button, the
  keys strip, a knob's row, the event line). But it does so for every
  event, and the script makes about 1 070 a second (840 encoder detents,
  200 pot steps, 32 key changes): about 66 000 instructions an event,
  mostly pixel-by-pixel fills and scaled glyphs into the 240 x 240 frame
  buffer. A key event repaints the whole 52-row keys strip.
- **It is already off the audio's critical path** in the sense that
  matters for underruns: drawing runs in main, at the lowest level, and
  the audio interrupt preempts it, so no block was late. What it costs is
  core 0's time, which M5's voices need, and under an overloaded engine
  main starves and the screen freezes.
- **What it would take, before M5** (not done; measure first):
  - **Coalesce:** mark regions dirty per event, and redraw at most once
    per frame, at a fixed rate (30 to 60 Hz), not once per event. At 1 070
    events a second against 60 frames, that is up to 18 times less: about
    6 000 a block under this load, if a frame redraws what one event does.
  - **Cheaper drawing:** fill whole words and rows (`gfx_fill` writes
    pairs of pixels today), and draw text from pre-rendered glyph rows at
    the scale used instead of pixel by pixel; redraw a knob's value, not
    its row.
  - **A drawing budget:** let main draw for at most a set share of each
    block (from the time base), carrying on next time, so the screen can
    never take what the voices need.
  - **Moving it:** core 1 could draw (the panel's DMA and its interrupt
    would move with it, and needs SR-6's answer about core 1's
    interrupts), but core 1 is worth a whole second core of voices
    (above), so coalescing on core 0 is the better first step.
- Re-measure with the loaded measure after any of these: the loaded gate
  (#57, #58) will show the change, and its budget can then come down.

### 2026-10-23 M4b: what the API should change before M5
- **An engine context.** `audio_engine_fn` takes no pointer, so an engine
  keeps its state in globals, and two voices on two cores can't share

  | Input scan (keys, encoders, pot, LEDs; LEDs 215 of it) | 1 861 | 1.6% |
  | Audio output path (the interrupt, its checks, the stores) | 302 | 0.3% |
  | The tick, main's wakes and the rest | 104 | 0.1% |
  | **Total** (114 173 by the record's count of blocks) | **114 117** | |

  The scan's share is the "no panel" build less the build with no scan as
  well, less the audio engine's (with no scan no note sounds).
- **The screen dominates, and it is the drawing, not the sending.** The
  panel already redraws only the region an event touches (a button, the
  keys strip, a knob's row, the event line). But it does so for every
  event, and the script makes about 1 070 a second (840 encoder detents,
  200 pot steps, 32 key changes): about 66 000 instructions an event,
  mostly pixel-by-pixel fills and scaled glyphs into the 240 x 240 frame
  buffer. A key event repaints the whole 52-row keys strip.
- **It is already off the audio's critical path** in the sense that
  matters for underruns: drawing runs in main, at the lowest level, and
  the audio interrupt preempts it, so no block was late. What it costs is
  core 0's time, which M5's voices need, and under an overloaded engine
  main starves and the screen freezes.
- **What it would take, before M5** (not done; measure first):
  - **Coalesce:** mark regions dirty per event, and redraw at most once
    per frame, at a fixed rate (30 to 60 Hz), not once per event. At 1 070
    events a second against 60 frames, that is up to 18 times less: about
    6 000 a block under this load, if a frame redraws what one event does.
  - **Cheaper drawing:** fill whole words and rows (`gfx_fill` writes
    pairs of pixels today), and draw text from pre-rendered glyph rows at
    the scale used instead of pixel by pixel; redraw a knob's value, not
    its row.
  - **A drawing budget:** let main draw for at most a set share of each
    block (from the time base), carrying on next time, so the screen can
    never take what the voices need.
  - **Moving it:** core 1 could draw (the panel's DMA and its interrupt
    would move with it, and needs SR-6's answer about core 1's
    interrupts), but core 1 is worth a whole second core of voices
    (above), so coalescing on core 0 is the better first step.
- Re-measure with the loaded measure after any of these: the loaded gate
  (#57, #58) will show the change, and its budget can then come down.

### 2026-10-23 M4b: what the API should change before M5
- **An engine context.** `audio_engine_fn` takes no pointer, so an engine
  keeps its state in globals, and two voices on two cores can't share

# The Plaits demo's own sources and the vendored Plaits (M4b,
# docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md): our C glue and runtime with the firmware's flags;
# our C++ with the same warnings, as errors (Plaits' headers are system
# headers to it: their warnings are not ours to fix); the vendored files
# unmodified at upstream's -O2, with warnings off. All the C++ is built in
# upstream's portable configuration (-DTEST), with our standard headers
# and plaits_pre.h in place of a C library's. Objects are named after their
# paths, since vendored names repeat.
build_demo_plaits() {
    d=firmware/demos/plaits
    CXX="clang -target pi32v2 -x c++ -std=c++11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -fno-exceptions
         -fno-rtti -fno-threadsafe-statics -fno-common -g -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
         -I$d/include -isystem vendor/plaits/eurorack -isystem vendor/plaits -I$d -Ifirmware/src
         -DTEST -include $d/include/plaits_pre.h"
    for d2 in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CXX="$CXX -D$d2"; done
    # PLAITS_HWFLOAT: the toolchain's hardware single-precision float
    # instructions (its fprev1 feature) instead of our soft-float, for the
    # C++ only: a measurement of what they would save, never the demo's
    # default, since whether the chip has them is open (SR-5).
    case " ${SB_DEFINES:-} " in
        *" PLAITS_HWFLOAT "*) CXX="$CXX -Xclang -target-feature -Xclang +fprev1" ;;
    esac
    defs=""
    for d2 in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do defs="$defs -D$d2"; done
    for s in $(find "$d" -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS $defs -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    for s in $(find "$d" -name '*.cc' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.cc$/.o/')"
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        set -x; $CXX -Os -Wall -Wextra -Werror -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    for s in $(find vendor/plaits -name '*.cc' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.cc$/.o/')"
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        $CXX -O2 -w -c "$s" -o "$o"
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    echo "built $(find vendor/plaits -name '*.cc' | wc -l) vendored Plaits files"
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.

# Requirements

Numbered requirements for this project (the original, MIT-licensed base
firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, JieLi AC791N). Every check names the
requirements it covers (`tools/record.py`, `CHECKS`), and every test record
ends with a traceability table: requirement → checks → result.

A requirement whose "Checked by" says *review* is checked by people when they
review a pull request, not by a machine. *Planned* means a later milestone
adds the check. The record lists both kinds, so nothing looks checked when it
isn't.

The four founding requirements (docs/prompts/M0a.md): **history**,
**tests**, **reproducible**, **public and efficient**.

| ID | Requirement | Since | Checked by |
|----|-------------|-------|------------|
| R-PROC-1 | Every commit message follows `.gitmessage` (subject `<area>: <summary>`; non-empty What, Why, How, Result, Sources, Exposure). Agent-written commits also carry `Model:` and `Claude-Session:` trailers. Merge commits are exempt; their pull request carries the sections. | M0a | C-COMMIT-MSG, C-UNIT |
| R-PROC-2 | main changes only through pull requests that passed CI, merged by the owner with a verified, signed merge commit (GitHub's merge button since 2026-10-22, CONTRIBUTING.md "Merge policy"). Nobody bypasses. No force pushes or deletion on main and `records`; `m*` tags are never moved or deleted. | M0a | rulesets (CONTRIBUTING.md); C-MERGE (records workflow) |
| R-PROC-3 | Each milestone's prompt is committed unedited in `docs/prompts/` in the commit that starts the milestone. | M0a | review |
| R-PROC-4 | Every check names the requirements it checks, and every record has a traceability table. | M0a | C-UNIT |
| R-REC-1 | Each commit pushed to main gets a permanent record `records/<sha>/` (report.json, report.md, logs) on the orphan `records` branch, written only by the records workflow, never for pull requests. A record is never changed: a later re-check of C-MERGE alone, started by hand with the merge check on main (`.github/workflows/recheck-merge.yml`), only adds `records/<sha>/verified-<date>/` beside it, naming the checker's commit and why. | M0a | records.yml; C-UNIT (record writer) |
| R-REC-2 | Each record has an OpenTimestamps proof. Upgraded proofs are added as new files and never replace the originals. | M0a | records.yml, ots-upgrade.yml |
| R-REPRO-1 | The toolchain is downloaded and checked against the SHA-256 in docs/TOOLCHAIN.md. It is never committed or published. | M0a | C-IMAGE, C-NO-TOOLCHAIN |
| R-REPRO-2 | The build container's base image is pinned by digest, its packages come from a pinned snapshot.debian.org date, and builds run under `linux/amd64` through `tools/build.sh`. | M0a | C-IMAGE |

Agent-written commits also carry `Model:` and `Claude-Session:` trailers. Merge commits are exempt; their pull request carries the sections. | M0a | C-COMMIT-MSG, C-UNIT |

42:| R-PUB-3 | No tracked file, commit message or archived transcript holds one of the owner's private terms (username, hostname, real e-mail, real name, local folder names), which live only in the gitignored `tools/[REDACTED:host]` and the `PRIVATE_TERMS` secret. A hit is reported by file and line only. A file under `sessions/` or `docs/prompts/` unchanged (same blob) since the base commit in `config/private-base` is exempt, decided from object hashes alone; everything added or changed after it is checked in full (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Privacy"). `tools/archive-session.py` redacts the username, the local top-level folder (as `<top>`) and the terms. The pre-commit and commit-msg hooks run the same check. Every record, audit report and re-check is scanned before it is hashed, uploaded or pushed: a file holding a term is withheld and listed, with the SHA-256 of the original, in `WITHHELD.json`, the rest is still written, and the check fails (since M1). | M0d | C-PRIVATE, C-RECORD-PRIVATE, C-UNIT; audit.yml, recheck-merge.yml |
48:| R-SEP-1 | Spec-side text discipline: what the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` only through `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` and `docs/HARNESS.md`. Spec-side commit messages, pull request texts and files elsewhere (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) carry no emulator internals (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Spec-side text discipline"). C-SEP-TERMS finds identifiers that occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in the files, commit messages and pull request texts the firmware side reads; people review `docs/HARNESS.md` and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. Since M4b (the owner's decision) the terms of `vendor/plaits/` (Plaits, MIT, R-REPRO-7) count as public like the SDK's: built only from the files its `SHA256SUMS` lists, each matching its hash, or the check fails; its log gives how many emulator terms that list takes off, as a count; and `vendor/plaits/` itself, third-party code we didn't write, is not scanned, except `vendor/plaits/SOURCE.md`, which we write (since SR-4). Universal constants are never terms (since SR-4's note, the owner's decision), defined by rule in the check, not by a list: powers of two (sign-bit masks among them), 2^n-1, 2^n+1, and IEEE 754's standard single and double patterns (infinities, quiet NaNs, one, 2^±23, 2^±52; the exponent biases and fraction masks are 2^n-1). | M0b, M4b, SR-4 | C-SEP-TERMS, C-UNIT; review |

- Facts: HW-62 (the SDK builds this chip's code with `-mcpu=r3

  is **byte for byte the same** (`app.bin` `543e5764...`, and the ELF):
  the firmware has no float yet, and the integer code `r3` gets is what
  the default gave. So the steady state (1 812.9 instructions a block),
  the loaded measure (114 172.7) and every size are unchanged. With the
  flag, a float operation is one instruction where it was a call into a
  float library (a test file: `a * b + a / b` became three instructions
  and a return, from two calls and their set-up).
- Fixed point stays where it is cheaper: M4's oscillator and mixing are
  32- and 64-bit integer multiplies, single instructions here (M4, P-27),
  with no conversions at the ends. Floats are for what fixed point makes
  awkward (wide-range values: rates, pitch ratios, envelope curves
  computed per block, not per sample). On the chip their cycle cost is
  still unknown (Q-16), so nothing per sample depends on a float.
- Alternatives: leaving the default CPU model (the same code today, but
  float would need a library); building only the engine with the flag
  (two ABIs to keep straight for no gain).
EOF

    `git push` of #57's branch tried to pack the branch's whole history
    and asked for a blob of a spec-side folder. Lazy fetching was off, so
    nothing was fetched and the push failed. To find the cause, a loop of
    `git ls-tree -r` over every local branch printed one spec-side file's
    path (a name, no contents). `tools/clean-update.sh` then brought main
    in and ended "no spec-side files on disk or in .git", and the push
    went through. Ref-wide tree listings are not to be repeated.
  - **Lazy fetching** was turned on only for scratch clones of upstream
    Plaits, stmlib and the SDK, command by command (as
    `tools/fetch-plaits.sh` does), never for this repository.
  - **Outside this folder, at the owner's request:** one built firmware

def beacon(data):

def elf_symbols(path):
    """name -> value, from an ELF32 little-endian file's symbol table."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        elf = f.read()
    shoff, = struct.unpack_from("<I", elf, 0x20)
    shentsize, shnum = struct.unpack_from("<HH", elf, 0x2E)
    sections = [struct.unpack_from("<IIIIIIIIII", elf, shoff + i * shentsize) for i in range(shnum)]
    syms = {}
    for s in sections:
        if s[1] != 2:      # SHT_SYMTAB
            continue
        strtab = sections[s[6]]
        for off in range(s[4], s[4] + s[5], 16):
            name, value = struct.unpack_from("<II", elf, off)
            end = elf.index(b"\0", strtab[4] + name)
            syms[elf[strtab[4] + name:end].decode()] = value
    return syms


def check_case(name, result):
    """Problems with one case's result.json."""
    run = result.get("run", {})
    problems = []
    if run.get("outcome") != EXPECT[name]:
        problems.append("%s: outcome %s, not %s (%s)" % (name, run.get("outcome"), EXPECT[name],
                                                         run.get("detail")))
    if run.get("unmodelled_accesses"):
        problems.append("%s: unmodelled accesses %s" % (name, run["unmodelled_accesses"]))
    if run.get("instructions", {}).get("core1", 0) != 0:
        problems.append("%s: core 1 ran" % name)
    return problems


def consistent(b):
    """The heartbeat copies that are consistent: [(beats, ticks), ...]."""
    return [(be, ti) for be, ti in ((b["beats"], b["ticks"]), (b["beats_b"], b["ticks_b"]))
            if be == ti // TICKS_PER_MS]


def start_slack(bss):
    """Time base ticks by which main may start the time base after fwtest's
    emulated time began: START_SLACK and the clearing of bss."""
    return START_SLACK + (bss // 4 * CLEAR_CYCLES_PER_WORD + 9) // 10


def check_beacon(when_ms, b, end_ms=None):
    """Problems with one beacon captured at when_ms (the time asked; end_ms
    is result.json's emulated_ms for the capture at the end)."""
    problems = []
    if b["marker"] != MARKER:
        problems.append("marker 0x%08x, not 0x%08x" % (b["marker"], MARKER))
    if b["period"] != TICKS_PER_MS:
        problems.append("period %d, not %d" % (b["period"], TICKS_PER_MS))
        return problems
    good = consistent(b)
    if not good:
        return problems + ["neither heartbeat copy is consistent: %d beats after %d ticks, %d after %d"
                           % (b["beats"], b["ticks"], b["beats_b"], b["ticks_b"])]
    if b["seq"] % 2 == 0 and (len(good) != 2 or good[0] != good[1]):
        problems.append("seq %d is even, but the two heartbeat copies differ" % b["seq"])
    ticks = good[-1][1]
    if end_ms is not None:
        end = round(end_ms * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not -START_SLACK <= end - ticks <= TICKS_PER_MS + INTERVAL_TOL + START_SLACK:
            problems.append("last tick at %d ticks, not within one tick period before the end (%d)"
                            % (ticks, end))
    else:
        low = round((when_ms - 1) * TICKS_PER_MS) - INTERVAL_TOL - START_SLACK
        high = round((when_ms + LATE_MS) * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not low <= ticks <= high:
            problems.append("%d ticks at %s ms, not within %d to %d" % (ticks, when_ms, low, high))
    return problems


def check_ticks(b, result):
    """Problems with the end beacon's tick statistics, and lines to print."""
    problems = []
    n, lo, hi = b["tick_count"], b["interval_min"], b["interval_max"]
    loop = b["wakes_ticks"] - b["loop_ticks"]
    lines = ["  ticks %d, interval %d to %d time base ticks (jitter %d); the idle loop's wait returned"
             " %d times in its first %d ticks" % (n, lo, hi, hi - lo, b["wakes"], loop)]
    if n < 2:
        return ["heartbeat: %d ticks" % n], lines
    for name, v in (("shortest", lo), ("longest", hi)):
        if abs(v - TICKS_PER_MS) > INTERVAL_TOL:
            problems.append("heartbeat: %s tick interval %d, not within %d of %d"
                            % (name, v, INTERVAL_TOL, TICKS_PER_MS))
    if hi - lo > INTERVAL_TOL:
        problems.append("heartbeat: tick jitter %d, more than %d" % (hi - lo, INTERVAL_TOL))
    beats = consistent(b)[-1][0] if consistent(b) else b["beats"]
    if abs(beats - n) > 1:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beats but %d ticks" % (beats, n))
    # Main counts its wakes in a register and stores the count with the
    # ticks taken whenever it has work (DESIGN-NOTES.md, M2 and M3). Since
    # M3 the scan wakes it too: at least once a tick, and at most once an
    # interrupt (the tick, SCAN_SLOTS scan slots, and an SPI1 transfer's
    # end a second), so it idles rather than spins.
    # Since M4 the audio output's blocks wake it too.
    most = (SCAN_SLOTS + 1) * (loop + 1) + loop // 1000 + 2 + loop * TICKS_PER_MS // BLOCK_TICKS + 2
    if not b["wakes_ticks"]:
        problems.append("heartbeat: main's idle loop never stored its wakes")
    elif not loop - 1 <= b["wakes"] <= most:
        problems.append("heartbeat: the idle wait returned %d times in %d ticks, not %d to %d"
                        % (b["wakes"], loop, loop - 1, most))
    return problems, lines


def check_steady(results, ends):
    """Steady-state instructions per tick, from the two heartbeat cases
    (the same options but their length: R-IRQ-1 since M2), and lines."""
    (r1, r2), (b1, b2) = results, ends
    i1, i2 = r1["run"]["instructions"]["core0"], r2["run"]["instructions"]["core0"]
    dn = b2["tick_count"] - b1["tick_count"]
    if dn <= 0:
        return ["heartbeat2: no more ticks than heartbeat"], []
    ipt = (i2 - i1) / dn
    lines = ["  steady state: %d instructions for %d ticks between the two heartbeat runs: %.3f a tick"
             " (M0's polling heartbeat: %.1f a period)" % (i2 - i1, dn, ipt, M0_IPP)]
    if ipt > IDLE_MAX_IPT:
        return ["heartbeat: %.1f instructions a tick in steady state, more than %d" % (ipt, IDLE_MAX_IPT)], lines
    return [], lines


def check_heartbeat(case_dir, result):
    """Problems with the heartbeat case's captures, and lines to print."""
    end_ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    caps = []
    for n in os.listdir(case_dir):
        m = CAPTURE.match(n)
        if m:
            when = m.group("when")
            caps.append((end_ms if when == "end" else float(when[:-2]), when, n))
    caps.sort()
    problems, lines, last, end = [], [], -1, None
    if len(caps) < 2:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beacon captures, expected several" % len(caps))
    for when_ms, when, n in caps:
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, n), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        if len(data) != BEACON_LEN:
            problems.append("%s: %d bytes" % (n, len(data)))
            continue
        b = beacon(data)
        lines.append("  %-6s seq %5d  beats %5d  ticks %9d (%.3f ms)  copy b %5d %9d"
                     % (when, b["seq"], b["beats"], b["ticks"], b["ticks"] / TICKS_PER_MS,
                        b["beats_b"], b["ticks_b"]))
        problems += ["heartbeat %s: %s" % (when, p) for p in
                     check_beacon(when_ms, b, end_ms if when == "end" else None)]
        good = consistent(b)
        if good and good[-1][0] < last:
            problems.append("heartbeat %s: beats went back from %d to %d" % (when, last, good[-1][0]))
        last = good[-1][0] if good else last
        if when == "end":
            end = b
    if end is not None:
        more, tick_lines = check_ticks(end, result)
        problems += more
        lines += tick_lines
    return problems, lines


def check_boot(case_dir, symbols):
    """Problems with the boot case's beacon and vector table, and lines."""
    problems, lines = [], []
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
        b = beacon(f.read())
    lines.append("  clock: %d time base ticks for 2402 cycles; %d ticks by the end"
                 % (b["clock"], b["tick_count"]))
    if b["marker"] != MARKER:
        problems.append("boot: marker 0x%08x" % b["marker"])
    if b["clock"] not in CLOCK_TICKS:
        problems.append("boot: the clock measured %d time base ticks, not %s (240 MHz)"
                        % (b["clock"], " or ".join(map(str, CLOCK_TICKS))))
    good = consistent(b)
    if b["tick_count"] < 1 or not good:
        problems.append("boot: no tick (or no consistent heartbeat) by the end")
    else:
        # No later than this: every interval is at least interval_min.
        first = good[-1][1] - (b["tick_count"] - 1) * b["interval_min"]
        lines.append("  first tick by %d time base ticks (%.3f ms)" % (first, first / TICKS_PER_MS))
        if first > FIRST_TICK_MS * TICKS_PER_MS:
            problems.append("boot: the first tick came after %.3f ms, not within %d ms"
                            % (first / TICKS_PER_MS, FIRST_TICK_MS))
    if b["halt_reason"]:
        problems.append("boot: halted (reason %d)" % b["halt_reason"])
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, VECTORS), "rb") as f:
        table = struct.unpack("<128I", f.read())
    want = [symbols["sb_irq_stubs"] + STUB_SIZE * n for n in range(128)]
    want[SRC_TICK] = symbols["sb_tick"]
    want[SRC_SPI1] = symbols["lcd_spi_done"]
    want[SRC_SCAN] = symbols["input_scan"]
    want[SRC_AUDIO] = symbols["audio_block"]
    wrong = [n for n in range(128) if table[n] != want[n]]
    lines.append("  vector table: %d of 128 slots as built (tick 0x%08x, SPI1 0x%08x, scan 0x%08x, audio 0x%08x,"
                 " stubs from 0x%08x)"
                 % (128 - len(wrong), symbols["sb_tick"], symbols["lcd_spi_done"], symbols["input_scan"],
                    symbols["audio_block"], symbols["sb_irq_stubs"]))

        problems.append("boot: vector table slots %s are not the handler built for them" % wrong)
    return problems, lines

    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
        b = beacon(f.read())
    line = "  halt: reason %d, source %d, reti 0x%08x" % (b["halt_reason"], b["halt_source"],
                                                          b["halt_reti"])

def read_png(path):
    """(width, height, rows of (r, g, b)) from an 8-bit RGB, non-interlaced
    PNG, as fwtest writes them (docs/HARNESS.md, lcd-WHEN.png)."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    if data[:8] != b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n":
        raise ValueError("not a PNG")
    pos, idat, w = 8, b"", None
    while pos < len(data):
        n, kind = struct.unpack_from(">I4s", data, pos)
        body = data[pos + 8:pos + 8 + n]
        if kind == b"IHDR":
            w, h, depth, ctype, _, _, interlace = struct.unpack(">IIBBBBB", body)
            if (depth, ctype, interlace) != (8, 2, 0):
                raise ValueError("not 8-bit RGB without interlace")
        elif kind == b"IDAT":
            idat += body
        pos += 12 + n
    raw, stride, rows, prev = zlib.decompress(idat), w * 3, [], bytearray(w * 3)
    for y in range(h):
        kind, line = raw[y * (stride + 1)], bytearray(raw[y * (stride + 1) + 1:(y + 1) * (stride + 1)])
        for i in range(stride):
            a = line[i - 3] if i >= 3 else 0
            b, c = prev[i], prev[i - 3] if i >= 3 else 0
            if kind == 1:
                line[i] = (line[i] + a) & 255
            elif kind == 2:
                line[i] = (line[i] + b) & 255
            elif kind == 3:
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a + b) // 2) & 255
            elif kind == 4:
                p = a + b - c
                pa, pb, pc = abs(p - a), abs(p - b), abs(p - c)
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a if pa <= pb and pa <= pc else b if pb <= pc else c)) & 255
        rows.append([tuple(line[i:i + 3]) for i in range(0, stride, 3)])
        prev = line
    return w, h, rows

                            % (name, v, INTERVAL_TOL, TICKS_PER_MS))
    if hi - lo > INTERVAL_TOL:
        problems.append("heartbeat: tick jitter %d, more than %d" % (hi - lo, INTERVAL_TOL))
    beats = consistent(b)[-1][0] if consistent(b) else b["beats"]
    if abs(beats - n) > 1:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beats but %d ticks" % (beats, n))
    # Main counts its wakes in a register and stores the count with the
    # ticks taken whenever it has work (DESIGN-NOTES.md, M2 and M3). Since
    # M3 the scan wakes it too: at least once a tick, and at most once an
    # interrupt (the tick, SCAN_SLOTS scan slots, and an SPI1 transfer's
    # end a second), so it idles rather than spins.
    # Since M4 the audio output's blocks wake it too.
    most = (SCAN_SLOTS + 1) * (loop + 1) + loop // 1000 + 2 + loop * TICKS_PER_MS // BLOCK_TICKS + 2
    if not b["wakes_ticks"]:
        problems.append("heartbeat: main's idle loop never stored its wakes")
    elif not loop - 1 <= b["wakes"] <= most:
        problems.append("heartbeat: the idle wait returned %d times in %d ticks, not %d to %d"
                        % (b["wakes"], loop, loop - 1, most))
    return problems, lines


def check_steady(results, ends):
    """Steady-state instructions per tick, from the two heartbeat cases
    (the same options but their length: R-IRQ-1 since M2), and lines."""
    (r1, r2), (b1, b2) = results, ends
    i1, i2 = r1["run"]["instructions"]["core0"], r2["run"]["instructions"]["core0"]
    dn = b2["tick_count"] - b1["tick_count"]
    if dn <= 0:
        return ["heartbeat2: no more ticks than heartbeat"], []
    ipt = (i2 - i1) / dn
    lines = ["  steady state: %d instructions for %d ticks between the two heartbeat runs: %.3f a tick"
             " (M0's polling heartbeat: %.1f a period)" % (i2 - i1, dn, ipt, M0_IPP)]
    if ipt > IDLE_MAX_IPT:
        return ["heartbeat: %.1f instructions a tick in steady state, more than %d" % (ipt, IDLE_MAX_IPT)], lines
    return [], lines


def check_heartbeat(case_dir, result):
    """Problems with the heartbeat case's captures, and lines to print."""
    end_ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    caps = []
    for n in os.listdir(case_dir):
        m = CAPTURE.match(n)
        if m:
            when = m.group("when")
            caps.append((end_ms if when == "end" else float(when[:-2]), when, n))
    caps.sort()
    problems, lines, last, end = [], [], -1, None
    if len(caps) < 2:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beacon captures, expected several" % len(caps))
    for when_ms, when, n in caps:
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, n), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        if len(data) != BEACON_LEN:
            problems.append("%s: %d bytes" % (n, len(data)))
            continue
        b = beacon(data)
        lines.append("  %-6s seq %5d  beats %5d  ticks %9d (%.3f ms)  copy b %5d %9d"
                     % (when, b["seq"], b["beats"], b["ticks"], b["ticks"] / TICKS_PER_MS,
                        b["beats_b"], b["ticks_b"]))
        problems += ["heartbeat %s: %s" % (when, p) for p in
                     check_beacon(when_ms, b, end_ms if when == "end" else None)]
        good = consistent(b)
        if good and good[-1][0] < last:
            problems.append("heartbeat %s: beats went back from %d to %d" % (when, last, good[-1][0]))
        last = good[-1][0] if good else last
        if when == "end":
            end = b
    if end is not None:
        more, tick_lines = check_ticks(end, result)
        problems += more
        lines += tick_lines
    return problems, lines


def check_boot(case_dir, symbols):
    """Problems with the boot case's beacon and vector table, and lines."""
    problems, lines = [], []
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
        b = beacon(f.read())
    lines.append("  clock: %d time base ticks for 2402 cycles; %d ticks by the end"
                 % (b["clock"], b["tick_count"]))
    if b["marker"] != MARKER:
        problems.append("boot: marker 0x%08x" % b["marker"])
    if b["clock"] not in CLOCK_TICKS:
        problems.append("boot: the clock measured %d time base ticks, not %s (240 MHz)"
                        % (b["clock"], " or ".join(map(str, CLOCK_TICKS))))
    good = consistent(b)
    if b["tick_count"] < 1 or not good:
        problems.append("boot: no tick (or no consistent heartbeat) by the end")
    else:
        # No later than this: every interval is at least interval_min.
        first = good[-1][1] - (b["tick_count"] - 1) * b["interval_min"]
        lines.append("  first tick by %d time base ticks (%.3f ms)" % (first, first / TICKS_PER_MS))
        if first > FIRST_TICK_MS * TICKS_PER_MS:
            problems.append("boot: the first tick came after %.3f ms, not within %d ms"
                            % (first / TICKS_PER_MS, FIRST_TICK_MS))
    if b["halt_reason"]:
        problems.append("boot: halted (reason %d)" % b["halt_reason"])
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, VECTORS), "rb") as f:
        table = struct.unpack("<128I", f.read())
    want = [symbols["sb_irq_stubs"] + STUB_SIZE * n for n in range(128)]
    want[SRC_TICK] = symbols["sb_tick"]
    want[SRC_SPI1] = symbols["lcd_spi_done"]
    want[SRC_SCAN] = symbols["input_scan"]
    want[SRC_AUDIO] = symbols["audio_block"]
    wrong = [n for n in range(128) if table[n] != want[n]]
    lines.append("  vector table: %d of 128 slots as built (tick 0x%08x, SPI1 0x%08x, scan 0x%08x, audio 0x%08x,"
                 " stubs from 0x%08x)"
                 % (128 - len(wrong), symbols["sb_tick"], symbols["lcd_spi_done"], symbols["input_scan"],
                    symbols["audio_block"], symbols["sb_irq_stubs"]))
    if wrong:
        problems.append("boot: vector table slots %s are not the handler built for them" % wrong)
    return problems, lines


def check_halt(name, case_dir, reason, source):
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
        b = beacon(f.read())
    line = "  halt: reason %d, source %d, reti 0x%08x" % (b["halt_reason"], b["halt_source"],
                                                          b["halt_reti"])
    if (b["halt_reason"], b["halt_source"]) != (reason, source):
        return ["%s: halted with reason %d source %d, not %d %d"
                % (name, b["halt_reason"], b["halt_source"], reason, source)], [line]
    return [], [line]


def read_png(path):
    """(width, height, rows of (r, g, b)) from an 8-bit RGB, non-interlaced
    PNG, as fwtest writes them (docs/HARNESS.md, lcd-WHEN.png)."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    if data[:8] != b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n":
        raise ValueError("not a PNG")
    pos, idat, w = 8, b"", None
    while pos < len(data):
        n, kind = struct.unpack_from(">I4s", data, pos)
        body = data[pos + 8:pos + 8 + n]
        if kind == b"IHDR":
            w, h, depth, ctype, _, _, interlace = struct.unpack(">IIBBBBB", body)
            if (depth, ctype, interlace) != (8, 2, 0):
                raise ValueError("not 8-bit RGB without interlace")
        elif kind == b"IDAT":
            idat += body
        pos += 12 + n
    raw, stride, rows, prev = zlib.decompress(idat), w * 3, [], bytearray(w * 3)
    for y in range(h):
        kind, line = raw[y * (stride + 1)], bytearray(raw[y * (stride + 1) + 1:(y + 1) * (stride + 1)])
        for i in range(stride):
            a = line[i - 3] if i >= 3 else 0
            b, c = prev[i], prev[i - 3] if i >= 3 else 0
            if kind == 1:
                line[i] = (line[i] + a) & 255
            elif kind == 2:
                line[i] = (line[i] + b) & 255
            elif kind == 3:
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a + b) // 2) & 255
            elif kind == 4:
                p = a + b - c
                pa, pb, pc = abs(p - a), abs(p - b), abs(p - c)
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a if pa <= pb and pa <= pc else b if pb <= pc else c)) & 255
        rows.append([tuple(line[i:i + 3]) for i in range(0, stride, 3)])
        prev = line
    return w, h, rows


def rgb8(r5, g6, b5):
    """The colour fwtest's PNG shows for an RGB565 pixel."""
    return (r5 * 255 // 31, g6 * 255 // 63, b5 * 255 // 31)


# screen.c's layouts (firmware/src/screen.c): where the test screen puts
# what, in pixels from the top left.
WHITE, RED, GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW = (rgb8(31, 63, 31), rgb8(31, 0, 0), rgb8(0, 63, 0),
                                   rgb8(0, 0, 31), rgb8(31, 63, 0))
CORNERS = (((3, 3), RED), ((225, 3), GREEN), ((3, 225), BLUE), ((225, 225), YELLOW))
BEAT_ROWS = range(200, 216)


def check_pattern(rows):
    """Problems with the address pattern: every pixel's colour must say
    where it is (screen.c's screen_pattern), so the orientation, the
    colour order and every pixel's address are checked at once."""
    bad = [(x, y) for y in range(240) for x in range(240)
           if rows[y][x] != rgb8(x >> 3, y >> 2, (x & 7) << 2 | (y & 3))]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Runs the firmware's fwtest suite and checks what it captured (check
C-FW-SUITE; R-BOOT-1 to R-BOOT-5, R-CLK-1, R-IRQ-1 to R-IRQ-4, R-LCD-1
to R-LCD-5, and since M3 R-KEY-1 to R-KEY-3, R-ENC-1, R-ENC-2, R-POT-1,
R-POT-2, R-LED-1 to R-LED-3, R-INPUT-1 to R-INPUT-3).

  fw-suite.py --build DIR --out DIR

Copies DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output) to out/fw/app.bin and builds
the test images (TEST_BUILDS: the same source with one SB_TEST_* define
each) to out/fw/<name>.bin, where tests/fw/boot.suite expects them, runs
the suite through tools/fwtest (the pinned image), and then checks:

- every case: the outcome the suite expects, no unmodelled accesses, core
  1 never ran;
- boot: the marker; the vector table, every slot (HW-18): source 4 is
  sb_tick, source 16 lcd_spi_done, source 5 input_scan (since M3), every
  other source its own stub in crt0.S, by the ELF's
  symbols; the clock measured at startup: SB_CLOCK_CYCLES core cycles take
  CLOCK_TICKS time base ticks (240 MHz against 24 MHz, HW-11, HW-13); the
  first tick within FIRST_TICK_MS of the start (from the last tick's time
  base, the ticks taken and the shortest interval, since the run itself
  ends late); nothing halted;
- heartbeat (one emulated second; the image idles between ticks, so
  captures come late, docs/HARNESS.md "Time"): at every capture at least
  one of the beacon's two heartbeat copies is consistent, beats ==
  ticks // 24000, and both are when its seq is even (the tick handler
  writes them in turn, DESIGN-NOTES.md M1); the consistent copy's ticks
  are no earlier than the time asked less one tick period and START_SLACK,
  and no more than LATE_MS after it; beats never go back. At the end:
  the last tick's time base lies within one tick period (and START_SLACK)
  before fwtest's emulated end time; every interval between two ticks is
  within INTERVAL_TOL of 24 000 time base ticks (1 ms), and so is their
  spread (jitter); beats and ticks taken differ by at most one; the idle
  wait returned at least once per tick and (since M3) at most once per
  interrupt, and core 0 ran at most IDLE_MAX_IPT instructions per tick
  (M0's polling heartbeat: M0_IPP per period);
- fault and stray: the halt recorded in the beacon (reason and source),
  and the console line, by golden file;
- badinsn: fwtest's own fault outcome for an undecodable instruction. A
  limit of the harness, not firmware behaviour: no handler of ours runs
  (SR-1).
- heartbeat2 (since M2): the heartbeat's checks again over 2.25 s; with
  heartbeat (1.25 s) its difference is the steady state, which may take
  at most IDLE_MAX_IPT instructions a tick. The idle loop's wakes, stored
  once a second, equal the ticks taken since it began, within one.
- screen (since M2): every pixel of the address pattern (300 ms) against
  its formula; the test screen's border, corners and ramps pixel by pixel
  (800 ms); one heartbeat later (1 500 ms) only the heartbeat's rows
  changed; the beacon's screen and seconds shown at each capture; and the
  three pictures against golden images.
- flood (since M2): a test build that sends whole frames back to back from
  500 ms: every tick interval still within INTERVAL_TOL, far more frames
  than ticks, and the picture still the test screen. Prints how long a
  whole frame takes.

- since M3, the panel (tests/fw/scripts/; docs/REQUIREMENTS.md has the
  limits): the input record after the beacon holds the counters, each
  control's value and the last 128 events, each stamped in time base ticks
  from when main started the time base. Each case's events (control, kind,
  value, never times) are compared with tests/fw/events/<case>.txt, and
  written as events.txt beside its outputs. Latencies run from the
  script's time of a change to the event's stamp, allowing for the time
  base starting anywhere within START_SLACK. keys: every key and button
  alone gives control n for fwtest key n, press and release, within
  KEY_LATENCY; its LED lit while held and dark otherwise (leds.csv), set
  within LED_LAG_MS of its event (the firmware's own measure). chords: no ghost, chatter and a glitch
  debounced, encoders exact with keys held in their columns, the panel
  screen against its golden image. encoders: slow detents within
  ENC_LATENCY, exact positions after fast, shared-column and all-at-once
  turns, and every tick interval within INTERVAL_TOL meanwhile. pot:
  steps within POT_FIRST and POT_SETTLED, one way each, no events at rest
  with noise, a rising sweep to 1023. leds (a test build): every LED at its
  brightness step within LED_STEP_TOL. ledshow (a test build, the keys
  script): from input_led to the scan first driving that LED, within
  LED_SHOW_MS (one scan).

Prints what it saw for the record, and exits 1 if anything failed.
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import zlib

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import audio_analysis as aa  # noqa: E402  (tools/, our own)

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SUITE = "tests/fw/boot.suite"
IMAGE = os.path.join("out", "fw", "app.bin")
# Test images: name -> define (firmware/src/probe.c).
TEST_BUILDS = {"test-fault": "SB_TEST_FAULT", "test-stray": "SB_TEST_STRAY",
               "test-badinsn": "SB_TEST_BADINSN", "test-flood": "SB_TEST_FLOOD",
               "test-leds": "SB_TEST_LEDS", "test-ledshow": "SB_TEST_LED_SHOW",
               "test-underrun": "SB_TEST_UNDERRUN"}
# Each case's expected outcome (the suite says the same; checked twice).
EXPECT = {"boot": "completed", "heartbeat": "completed", "heartbeat2": "completed",
          "screen": "completed", "flood": "completed", "fault": "halt", "stray": "halt",
          "badinsn": "fault", "keys": "completed", "chords": "completed", "encoders": "completed",
          "pot": "completed", "leds": "completed", "ledshow": "completed",
          "tone": "completed", "notes": "completed", "audioload": "completed",
          "audiogold": "completed", "underrun": "completed"}

MARKER = 0x44304253        # "SB0D", firmware/src/sb.h
TICKS_PER_MS = 24000       # HW-13
START_SLACK = 240          # ticks: 10 microseconds (main starts the time base)
# Startup clears .bss before main starts the time base, at most this many
# core cycles a word (2 measured in M2), 10 cycles a time base tick: since
# M2's frame buffer that is about a quarter of a millisecond, so the slack
# grows with the image's bss (start_slack).
CLEAR_CYCLES_PER_WORD = 3
LATE_MS = 30               # a waiting core 0 crosses many ticks in one run
INTERVAL_TOL = 24          # ticks: 1 microsecond, 0.1% of a tick period
CLOCK_TICKS = (240, 241)   # SB_CLOCK_CYCLES = 2402 cycles at 10 a tick
FIRST_TICK_MS = 2          # the first tick: one period after main starts it
IDLE_MAX_IPT = 1536        # instructions per tick, in steady state (since M2;
                           # 100 until M3's scanning, 1 280 until M4's audio:
                           # DESIGN-NOTES.md, M3 and M4)
SCAN_SLOTS = 12            # input scan interrupts a tick (input.c, since M3)
M0_IPP = 356.887           # M0's instructions per period (its last record)
STUB_SIZE = 2              # crt0.S's sb_irq_stubs
SRC_TICK = 4               # TIMER0 (HW-16, HW-19)
SRC_SPI1 = 16              # SPI1, the panel's transfers (HW-29)
SRC_SCAN = 5               # TIMER1, the input scan (HW-48, since M3)
HALT_STRAY, HALT_FAULT, HALT_STACK = 1, 2, 3

BEACON_FIELDS = ("marker", "beats", "ticks", "period", "seq", "beats_b", "ticks_b",
                 "tick_count", "interval_min", "interval_max", "wakes", "clock",
                 "halt_reason", "halt_source", "halt_reti",
                 # since M2 (firmware/src/sb.h)
                 "screen", "loop_ticks", "frames", "frame_ticks", "render_ticks", "beat_ticks",
                 "shown", "chunks", "wakes_ticks")

# through tools/fwtest, and then checks the captures: its docstring says how.
#
# boot (R-BOOT-1, R-BOOT-4, R-BOOT-5, R-CLK-1, R-IRQ-1, R-IRQ-2): main runs,
#   writes the marker and the console line, measures the clock and starts
#   the tick; RAM from 0x01c7fc00 to the vector table is as fwtest started
#   it (the r0 block, then zeros): golden files, exact. The beacon and the
#   vector table are checked by tools/fw-suite.py (the table against the
#   ELF's symbols, so a code change doesn't need a new golden file).
# heartbeat, heartbeat2 (R-BOOT-2, R-BOOT-3, R-BOOT-4, R-IRQ-1, R-IRQ-2):
#   1.25 and 2.25 s on the tick, the beacon captured along the way; the
#   watchdog fails the run if the beat count stops for 5 ms. The two differ
#   only in length, so their difference is the steady state (since M2).

#   screen at 800 ms and, one heartbeat later, at 1 500 ms: golden images,
#   exact, and tools/fw-suite.py checks every pixel of the pattern and the
#   test screen's border, corners and ramps on its own.
# flood (R-LCD-5): a test build sends whole frames back to back once the
#   test screen is up; every tick must keep its timing.
# fault (R-IRQ-4): a test build overruns main's stack; the next tick finds
#   the guard overwritten, reports it on the console and halts.
# stray (R-IRQ-3): a test build raises an interrupt nothing handles; its
#   stub reports the source on the console and halts.

#   instruction ends the run with fwtest's own fault, before any handler of

def check_pot(case_dir):
    """Steps, ends, noise at rest and a sweep (tests/fw/scripts/pot.txt)."""
    _, _, log = input_record(os.path.join(case_dir, input_name("960ms")))
    problems = check_events("pot", case_dir, log)
    lines = []
    for step, target in ((700, 300), (750, 0), (800, 1023), (850, 512)):
        ev = [(v, t) for _, c, k, v, t in log if c == MASTER and step * TICKS_PER_MS - START_SLACK <= t < (step + 49) * TICKS_PER_MS]
        if not ev:
            problems.append("pot: no event after the step to %d at %d ms" % (target, step))
            continue
        first, last = latency(ev[0][1], step), latency(ev[-1][1], step)
        lines.append("  step to %4d at %d ms: %d events, the first %.3f to %.3f ms after, %d reached %.3f to %.3f ms after"
                     % (target, step, len(ev), first[0], first[1], ev[-1][0], last[0], last[1]))
        vals = [v for v, _ in ev]
        if vals != sorted(vals) and vals != sorted(vals, reverse=True):
            problems.append("pot: the step to %d went both ways: %s" % (target, vals))
        if ev[-1][0] != target or first[1] > POT_FIRST or last[1] > POT_SETTLED:
            problems.append("pot: the step to %d gave %s, first within %.3f ms, last within %.3f (limits %s, %s)"
                            % (target, [v for v, _ in ev], first[1], last[1], POT_FIRST, POT_SETTLED))
    noise = [e for e in log if e[1] == MASTER and e[4] >= 899 * TICKS_PER_MS]
    if noise:
        problems.append("pot: %d events while the reading wandered by 2 at rest" % len(noise))
    head, values, log = input_record(os.path.join(case_dir, input_name("end")))
    sweep = [v for _, c, k, v, t in log if c == MASTER and t >= 999 * TICKS_PER_MS]
    if sweep != sorted(sweep) or values[MASTER] != 1023 or head["dropped"]:
        problems.append("pot: the sweep gave %s ... ending at %d, not rising to 1023 (%d dropped)"
                        % (sweep[:8], values[MASTER], head["dropped"]))
    lines.append("  no events while the reading wandered by 2 at rest; the sweep rose in %d events to %d"
                 % (len(sweep), values[MASTER]))
    return problems, lines

# synth.c; docs/REQUIREMENTS.md R-AUD-*). The sound is measured by our own
# analysis (tools/audio_analysis.py), at the output's true rate.
AUDIO_ADDR, AUDIO_LEN = 0x01c00550, 0x40
AUDIO_FIELDS = ("marker", "start", "blocks", "underruns", "fill_last", "fill_max", "dropped",
                "voices_on", "notes", "tone", "master", "taken", "stolen", "octave", "first_on",
                "last_off")                                   # audio.h's order
AUDIO_MARKER = 0x34445541  # "AUD4"
SRC_AUDIO = 11             # the audio link (HW-19, HW-43)
BLOCK_TICKS = aa.BLOCK * 544   # time base ticks a block (HW-45): 1.451 ms
HELLO = "small-beeps M4 \n"
# Limits (docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, R-AUD-4 to R-AUD-6).
TONE_HZ, TONE_DBFS = 1000.0, 20 * math.log10(0.5)
TONE_CENTS, NOTE_CENTS = 0.05, 0.1
LEVEL_DB = 0.1
TONE_THDN_DB, NOTE_THDN_DB = -85.0, -70.0
ATTACK_SAMPLES, RELEASE_SAMPLES = 221, 882   # the instrument's ramps (synth.c)
SOUND_FROM_KEY = (2.5, 7.5)     # ms from the key's contact to its first sample
SOUND_FROM_EVENT = 2 * BLOCK_TICKS / TICKS_PER_MS + 0.2   # ms: two blocks, and 0.2
SILENCE_RUN = 200               # zero samples in a row that end a sound


def audio_record(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        return dict(zip(AUDIO_FIELDS, struct.unpack("<%dI" % len(AUDIO_FIELDS), f.read()[:AUDIO_LEN])))


def audio_name(when="end"):
    return "ram-%08x-%x-%s.bin" % (AUDIO_ADDR, AUDIO_LEN, when)


def check_audio_common(name, case_dir, underruns=0):
    """Every audio case: the output ran, each block was filled once, the
    console holds nothing but the start line (and the underruns expected),
    and the WAV is mono in stereo (left equals right). Returns (problems,
    lines, record, wav) where wav is (left, block ends) or None."""
    problems, lines = [], []
    a = audio_record(os.path.join(case_dir, audio_name()))
    ends = aa.read_ipb(os.path.join(case_dir, "ipb.csv"))
    if a["marker"] != AUDIO_MARKER:
        problems.append("%s: the audio record's marker is 0x%08x" % (name, a["marker"]))
    # The end capture can come while the last block's fill is still going.
    if not len(ends) - 1 <= a["blocks"] <= len(ends):
        problems.append("%s: %d blocks filled, fwtest finished %d" % (name, a["blocks"], len(ends)))
    if a["underruns"] != underruns:
        problems.append("%s: %d underruns, expected %d" % (name, a["underruns"], underruns))
    if a["dropped"]:
        problems.append("%s: the engine's queue dropped %d events" % (name, a["dropped"]))
    gaps = [i for i in range(1, len(ends)) if not 0 < ends[i] - ends[i - 1] < 2 * BLOCK_TICKS / TICKS_PER_MS]
    if gaps:
        problems.append("%s: blocks %s ended more than a block after the one before" % (name, gaps[:5]))
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "console.txt")) as f:
        console = f.read()
    if not console.startswith(HELLO):
        problems.append("%s: the console doesn't start with the start line" % name)
    lines.append("  audio: %d blocks filled (fwtest: %d), %d underruns, longest fill %.1f us, "
                 "%d events to the engine"
                 % (a["blocks"], len(ends), a["underruns"], a["fill_max"] / 24.0, a["taken"]))
    wav = None
    path = os.path.join(case_dir, "audio.wav")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        rate, left, right = aa.read_wav(path)
        if left != right:
            problems.append("%s: left and right differ" % name)
        if len(left) != aa.BLOCK * len(ends):
            problems.append("%s: %d samples for %d blocks" % (name, len(left), len(ends)))
        lines.append("  audio.wav: %d frames (header %d Hz; measured at %.3f Hz)" % (len(left), rate, aa.RATE))
        wav = (left, ends)
    return problems, lines, a, console, wav


def sounds(x):
    """[(first, last)] sample of each sound: from a non-zero sample to the
    last before SILENCE_RUN zeros."""
    out, i, n = [], 0, len(x)
    while i < n:
        while i < n and not x[i]:
            i += 1
        if i >= n:
            break
        first, zeros, j = i, 0, i
        while j < n and zeros < SILENCE_RUN:
            zeros = zeros + 1 if not x[j] else 0
            j += 1
        out.append((first, j - zeros - 1))
        i = j
    return out


def check_clicks(name, x, first, last, fit):
    """No click where a sound starts and stops: the largest second
    difference over the attack and the release within click_bound."""
    a, f = fit["amplitude"], fit["frequency"]
    problems = []
    for what, lo, hi, ramp in (("start", first - 50, first + ATTACK_SAMPLES + 50, ATTACK_SAMPLES),
                               ("stop", last - RELEASE_SAMPLES - 150, last + 50, RELEASE_SAMPLES)):
        d2 = aa.max_second_difference(x[max(0, lo):hi])
        bound = aa.click_bound(a, f, ramp)
        if d2 > bound:
            problems.append("%s: a click at the %s of the sound at sample %d: second difference %d, "
                            "more than %.1f" % (name, what, first if what == "start" else last, d2, bound))
    return problems


def check_tone(case_dir):
    """The test tone (tests/fw/scripts/tone.txt): frequency, level, THD+N,
    a clean start and stop, and digital silence at rest around it."""
    problems, lines, a, _, wav = check_audio_common("tone", case_dir)
    if wav is None:
        return problems + ["tone: no audio.wav"], lines
    x, ends = wav
    s = sounds(x)
    if len(s) != 1:
        return problems + ["tone: %d sounds, expected one" % len(s)], lines
    first, last = s[0]
    fit = aa.sine_fit(x[int(0.5 * aa.RATE):int(2.2 * aa.RATE)])
    c, lvl, thdn = aa.cents(fit["frequency"], TONE_HZ), aa.dbfs(fit["amplitude"]), aa.thd_n_db(fit)
    lines.append("  test tone: %.6f Hz (%+.5f cents), %.3f dBFS, THD+N %.1f dB, from %.3f to %.3f ms;"
                 " silence (every sample 0) before and after"
                 % (fit["frequency"], c, lvl, thdn, aa.sample_ms(first, ends), aa.sample_ms(last, ends)))
    if abs(c) > TONE_CENTS:
        problems.append("tone: %.6f Hz, %+.4f cents from %s Hz (at most %s)" % (fit["frequency"], c, TONE_HZ, TONE_CENTS))
    if abs(lvl - TONE_DBFS) > LEVEL_DB:
        problems.append("tone: %.3f dBFS, not within %s dB of %.3f" % (lvl, LEVEL_DB, TONE_DBFS))
    if thdn > TONE_THDN_DB:
        problems.append("tone: THD+N %.1f dB, above %s" % (thdn, TONE_THDN_DB))
    problems += check_clicks("tone", x, first, last, fit)
    on = aa.sample_ms(first, ends)
    if not SOUND_FROM_KEY[0] <= on - 100 <= SOUND_FROM_KEY[1]:
        problems.append("tone: began %.3f ms after PLAY, not within %s" % (on - 100, SOUND_FROM_KEY))
    return problems, lines

    """synth.c's MASTER law: the square of its position, full at 1023."""
    return 1.0 if pot >= 1023 else pot * pot * 16 / float(1 << 24)

"""Our own analysis of fwtest's audio captures (M4; tools/fw-suite.py,
R-AUD-*). Python's standard library only: `wave` reads the file, the rest
is written here (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M4, "How the sound is measured").

- The rate: fwtest's WAV header says 44 100 Hz, but the output plays a
  frame every 544 ticks of 24 MHz (HW-45), 44 117.647 Hz; every
  frequency here is computed at that rate (RATE).
- sine_fit: a four-parameter least-squares fit of a sine (amplitude,
  phase, offset and frequency), refined by Gauss-Newton steps from a
  first guess counted from zero crossings. Its frequency is the
  measurement; its residual is THD+N's distortion and noise.
- clicks: the largest second difference of the samples, against what a
  sine of that amplitude and frequency can give under the instrument's
  linear ramps. A step (a hard start or stop) gives a second difference
  of about the step itself, many times the bound.
"""
import math
import struct
import wave

RATE = 24000000 / 544          # frames a second (HW-45)
FULL = 32768                   # 16-bit full scale in the WAV
BLOCK = 64                     # stereo frames a block (firmware/src/audio.h)


def read_wav(path):
    """(header rate, left, right) of a 16-bit stereo WAV."""
    with wave.open(path, "rb") as w:
        if w.getsampwidth() != 2 or w.getnchannels() != 2:
            raise ValueError("%s: not 16-bit stereo" % path)
        n = w.getnframes()
        data = struct.unpack("<%dh" % (2 * n), w.readframes(n))
        return w.getframerate(), list(data[0::2]), list(data[1::2])


def read_ipb(path):
    """The time each audio block ended, in ms, by block number (ipb.csv)."""
    with open(path) as f:
        rows = [l.strip().split(",") for l in f if l.strip()][1:]
    return [float(r[1]) for r in rows]


def sample_ms(n, ends):
    """When sample n began to play, in ms of emulated time: its block
    ended at ends[n // BLOCK], and its frames played one after another up
    to then."""
    return ends[n // BLOCK] - (BLOCK - n % BLOCK) * 1000.0 / RATE


def crossings(x):
    """Rising zero crossings, as fractional sample indices."""
    out = []
    for i in range(1, len(x)):
        if x[i - 1] < 0 <= x[i] and x[i] != x[i - 1]:
            out.append(i - 1 + (-x[i - 1]) / (x[i] - x[i - 1]))
    return out


def solve(m, v):
    """Solves the small linear system m x = v (Gaussian elimination)."""
    n = len(v)
    a = [list(m[i]) + [v[i]] for i in range(n)]
    for c in range(n):
        p = max(range(c, n), key=lambda r: abs(a[r][c]))
        a[c], a[p] = a[p], a[c]
        if a[c][c] == 0:
            raise ValueError("singular fit")
        for r in range(n):
            if r != c:
                f = a[r][c] / a[c][c]
                a[r] = [x - f * y for x, y in zip(a[r], a[c])]
    return [a[i][n] / a[i][i] for i in range(n)]


def sine_fit(x, rate=RATE, iterations=8):
    """{amplitude, frequency, phase, offset, residual}: the least-squares
    sine through samples x (residual: the RMS of what is left)."""
    c = crossings(x)
    if len(c) < 3:
        raise ValueError("too few cycles to fit")
    f = (len(c) - 1) / (c[-1] - c[0]) * rate
    t0 = len(x) / 2.0
    ts = [(i - t0) / rate for i in range(len(x))]
    a = b = d = 0.0
    for it in range(iterations):
        w = 2 * math.pi * f
        cs = [math.cos(w * t) for t in ts]
        sn = [math.sin(w * t) for t in ts]
        if it == 0:
            cols = [cs, sn, [1.0] * len(x)]
        else:
            cols = [cs, sn, [1.0] * len(x), [t * (-a * s + b * co) for t, s, co in zip(ts, sn, cs)]]
        m = [[sum(p * q for p, q in zip(ci, cj)) for cj in cols] for ci in cols]
        v = [sum(p * q for p, q in zip(ci, x)) for ci in cols]
        sol = solve(m, v)
        a, b, d = sol[0], sol[1], sol[2]
        if it:
            f += sol[3] / (2 * math.pi)
    w = 2 * math.pi * f
    res = [xi - (a * math.cos(w * t) + b * math.sin(w * t) + d) for xi, t in zip(x, ts)]
    return {"amplitude": math.hypot(a, b), "frequency": f, "phase": math.atan2(-b, a),
            "offset": d, "residual": math.sqrt(sum(r * r for r in res) / len(res))}


def thd_n_db(fit):
    """THD+N in dB: what the fitted sine leaves, against the sine (RMS)."""
    return 20 * math.log10(fit["residual"] / (fit["amplitude"] / math.sqrt(2)))


def dbfs(amplitude):
    """A sine's peak amplitude in dB of 16-bit full scale."""
    return 20 * math.log10(amplitude / FULL)


def cents(f, ref):
    return 1200 * math.log2(f / ref)


def note_hz(note):
    """Equal temperament, A4 (MIDI 69) = 440 Hz."""
    return 440.0 * 2 ** ((note - 69) / 12.0)


def max_second_difference(x):
    return max((abs(x[i] - 2 * x[i - 1] + x[i - 2]) for i in range(2, len(x))), default=0)


def click_bound(amplitude, f, ramp, rate=RATE, quantum=4):
    """The largest second difference a sine of this amplitude and
    frequency can show under a linear ramp of `ramp` samples (its own
    curvature, plus the ramp's corner and its slope against the sine's),
    and a few steps of the WAV's rounding."""
    w = 2 * math.pi * f / rate

AUDIO_ADDR, AUDIO_LEN = 0x01c00550, 0x40
AUDIO_FIELDS = ("marker", "start", "blocks", "underruns", "fill_last", "fill_max", "dropped",
                "voices_on", "notes", "tone", "master", "taken", "stolen", "octave", "first_on",
                "last_off")                                   # audio.h's order
AUDIO_MARKER = 0x34445541  # "AUD4"
SRC_AUDIO = 11             # the audio link (HW-19, HW-43)

LEVEL_DB = 0.1
TONE_THDN_DB, NOTE_THDN_DB = -85.0, -70.0
